Fig. 1:Representative universal image restoration frameworks.
(a) Degradation-agnostic methods use a shared backbone without explicit degradation conditioning.
Degradation-aware methods guide restoration through conditioning (b) or expert-based processing (c) that routes features toward degradation-specific experts.
These representative methods typically use a fixed degradation granularity, which can make them sensitive to degradation-estimation errors.
(d) UniRestorer+⁣+++proposes multi-granularity degradation modeling, expanding model capacity by introducing finer degradation-specific restoration experts. Degradation-estimation-based routing determines a hierarchical path, while granularity-estimation-based routing selects an expert level along that path, balancing degradation-specific specialization with robustness to degradation-estimation errors.

Fig. 3:Universal restoration performance on single-degradation tasks, CDD-11, CDD-50, and real-world datasets.

Fig. 4:Overview of UniRestorer+⁣+++. Globally pooled degradation representations (DRs) are hierarchically clustered to construct a multi-granularity degradation set, while dense DR maps are retained for region-aware expert routing. At each restoration block, the degradation-estimation-based and granularity-estimation-based routers are conditioned on both dense DR priors and the current restoration feature, enabling expert routing to adapt throughout the network. Their joint decision produces an expert assignment at each spatial location.
Fig. 5:Illustration of the degradation pipeline. Weather artifacts are first introduced, after which the remaining degradation types are randomly selected, shuffled, and sequentially applied.

Fig. 6:Visual comparison across the single-degradation (GoPro deblurring), triple-degradation (CDD-11), penta-degradation (CDD-50), and real-world settings. UniRestorer+⁣+++removes degradations and recovers textures and colors, as highlighted by thered boxesand enlarged regions.
Fig. 7:Visual comparison of zero-shot and five-shot UniRestorer+⁣+++against specialist models. Five-shot fine-tuning improves degradation removal and detail recovery, as highlighted by thered boxes.

Left: degradation-estimation-based router (DER) assignments to the eight finest-level DR groups, whose dominant degradation types are shown on the horizontal axis. Right: granularity-estimation-based router (GER) assignments to the hierarchy levels. Rows correspond to the 11 CDD-11 degradation subsets.

Fig. 10:Visualization of the dense DR map for real-world spatially varying degradations,i.e., motion blur (ReLoBlur[90]), defocus blur (DPDD[84]), and haze (FoundIR[30]). Gray and black indicate relatively lower and higher degradation severity, respectively.
